title: Predictive Fleet Fence with Staged Priority Shedder
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware, predictive admission controller ("Fence") that integrates short-horizon workload forecasts with staged priority shedding. The goal is to guarantee minimum throughput for committed tenants while improving overall fleet utilization and reducing tail latency during bursty inputs. This ticket covers forecasting integration, windowed admission decisions, staged shedding policies (soft degrade -> hard shed), and observability hooks for rollback and post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: The Fence uses a 30s forecast window (configurable) to preemptively reserve throughput per-tenant and avoid reactive overloads
Committed tenants receive a deterministic min-throughput allocation under normal and degraded modes (unit tests and bench validated)
Staged shedding executes in two phases: soft-degrade (priority demotion + reduced batch size) followed by hard-shed (reject with 429 or graceful fallback) when headroom is exhausted
End-to-end e2e tests demonstrating <5% error increase for best-effort customers and preserved 99th latency SLO for P1 tenants under synthetic 2x burst traffic
Console dashboard surfaces per-tenant reserved capacity, forecast delta, shed events, and recommended rollback actions
Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be rolled back to current admission logic with zero data migrations
technical_design: Overview: The Fence is a thin admission proxy at fleet ingress that consults three inputs: current utilization, short-horizon workload forecast (15-60s), and tenant SLAs. Forecasting: integrate a lightweight ARIMA-lite model produced by the workload-predictor service (gRPC endpoint) with a fallback to moving-average if predictor is unavailable. Decision windowing: admission decisions are computed on sliding 10s windows with hysteresis to avoid oscillation. Allocation model: deterministic reservation per-tenant expressed as tokens/sec with a soft buffer percentage. Staged shedding: Phase 1 (soft): mark requests as 'degraded' — reduce batch size, enable lower-cost quantized model variant, and set lowered internal priority; Phase 2 (hard): issue explicit reject with structured payload that includes fallback hints and estimated retry-after. Safety: graceful drain allowing in-flight KV cache reuse, and a circuit that disables forecasting if prediction error > 40% for 3 consecutive windows. Observability: histogram of forecast error, per-tenant shed counts, and end-to-end tracing linking admission decision to final response type. Telemetry will include recommended manual overrides for ops. Performance: admission path must add <1ms p95 overhead; microbenchmarks required. Backwards compatibility: expose a compatibility mode mapping old admission keys to the new reservation API. Security: ensure forecasting calls are authenticated via mTLS and do not leak tenant IDs in logs.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary behind config flag in a single region on small dedicated pool (week 0) 2) Monitor forecast error, shed rate, latency SLOs for 48 hours 3) Expand to 10% fleet if stable for 72 hours 4) Full rollout with opt-in per-tenant controls and throttle knobs (2 weeks) 5) Post-rollout review and tuning. Rollback path: disable flag to revert to current admission proxy; we will maintain historical metrics for postmortem.
tasks: Define forecasting contract with workload-predictor team (gRPC proto and SLA)
Implement Fence admission module in ingress service (Go) with token reservation and windowing
Add staged shedding handlers and structured reject payloads
Integrate with console: per-tenant reservation UI and shed event dashboard
Add end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (delayed forecasts, prediction spikes)
Load test with dedicated-pool-sim harness and validate p95 overhead <1ms
Security review and mTLS cert provisioning for predictor integration
Write runbook and rollback playbook for SREs
